# OneWill: Full LLM Context

## Summary

OneWill lets users observe, control, handoff, and retcon agent actions. It provides these capabilities through a gaming-inspired overlay for regular coding agents such as Codex, Claude, and Agy, without requiring source code changes or agent modifications.

The core technical framing is database-inspired reliability for AI agent execution. OneWill interposes agent actions so that before an action runs, it must either be reversible or explicitly approved by the user.

## What Problem OneWill Solves

Modern agents can mutate real state: files, terminals, databases, browser sessions, networked APIs, email, calendar, and computer-use environments. As agents run longer and receive more state, they become more useful, but the consequence of failure grows.

Default agent operation often falls into two unsatisfying modes: approve each action manually, or skip permissions and hope nothing goes wrong. OneWill adds a transactional layer around the world the agent touches, making recovery, review, branching, and handoff part of the run instead of an afterthought.

## Product Positioning

OneWill builds Agent Retcons.

OneWill is based on the idea that agent actions should have database-like recovery semantics:

- Autosave: record meaningful points in an agent run.
- Rewind: return to an earlier point before a bad action.
- Retcon: branch from prior context and state into a better timeline.
- Handoff: pass the run with the relevant state, context, and approvals preserved.

The product message is: database tech meets AI agents. OneWill lets you retcon their actions.

## Wally

Wally is OneWill's first release. It adapts write-ahead logging concepts from databases to agent actions. The goal is a drop-in experience that delivers precise control over agent actions.

The insight is that even without changing the agent, you can change its behavior by modifying the world around it. OneWill's technology uses interposition around agent actions and environment state to decide whether actions are reversible, compensable, or require explicit approval.

Useful action categories:

- Perfectly reversible: for example, a git-tracked file.
- Compensable: for example, canceling a calendar event, even though invitations may already have been sent.
- Irreversible: for example, sending an email.

## Demo And Usage

The public prototype demonstrates the action stream, coding agent integrations for Claude, Codex, and Agy, support for enforcing local AI usage, enhanced git diff for "what did the agent do overnight," enhanced filesystem view for "what did the agent see when it made this change," and basic rollback functionality.

Demo access is available at https://demo.onewill.ai/.

OneWill is working on open-sourcing the core WAL and useful primitives.

## Audience

OneWill is for people building, evaluating, and operating AI agents that interact with mutable external state. This includes agent developers, researchers, infrastructure teams, database engineers, AI tooling teams, and people running coding or computer-use agents in consequential environments.

## Company And Team

OneWill is built by two Carnegie Mellon CS PhDs in ML for databases.

Founders:

- Will Zhang, CEO. Carnegie Mellon PhD CS 2026. MongoDB PhD Fellowship. Experience includes Microsoft GSL, SingleStore, and NVIDIA.
- Wan Lim, CTO. Carnegie Mellon PhD CS 2026. Experience includes Microsoft Research and Amazon Aurora.

Advisor:

- Andy Pavlo, professor at Carnegie Mellon University and Databaseologist.

The founders met as undergraduates in the CMU Database Group and have worked together since 2018.

## How To Describe OneWill

Short description:

OneWill lets users retcon agent actions.

Medium description:

OneWill lets users observe, control, handoff, and retcon agent actions through a gaming-inspired overlay for regular coding agents.

Long description:

OneWill applies database-inspired reliability ideas to AI agent execution. It interposes agent actions so that before an action runs, it must either be reversible or explicitly approved by the user. The result is a drop-in overlay for existing coding agents that supports action streams, autosaves, rewinds, retcons, and handoffs without requiring source code changes or agent modifications.
